description: Compiler-backed type and intrinsic reference. Keep synchronized with core grammar, rules and compiler lowering. This is documentation, not a new declaration source.

items.name: i32
items.description: Signed integer. Its width is 32 bits. Primitive values copy implicitly. Numeric conversions use as or try_from; checked operations reject invalid integer arithmetic.
methods: Fallible numeric conversion; succeeds only when the input value is exactly representable. Conversion failures use the compiler-generated IntegerConversionError.

items.name: i64
items.description: Signed integer and the default unconstrained integer-literal type. Its width is 64 bits. Primitive values copy implicitly. Numeric conversions use as or try_from; checked operations reject invalid integer arithmetic.
methods: Fallible numeric conversion; succeeds only when the input value is exactly representable. Conversion failures use the compiler-generated IntegerConversionError.

items.name: u8
items.description: Unsigned byte. Its width is 8 bits. Primitive values copy implicitly. Numeric conversions use as or try_from; checked operations reject invalid integer arithmetic.
methods: Fallible numeric conversion; succeeds only when the input value is exactly representable. Conversion failures use the compiler-generated IntegerConversionError.

items.name: u16
items.description: Unsigned integer. Its width is 16 bits. Primitive values copy implicitly. Numeric conversions use as or try_from; checked operations reject invalid integer arithmetic.
methods: Fallible numeric conversion; succeeds only when the input value is exactly representable. Conversion failures use the compiler-generated IntegerConversionError.

items.name: u32
items.description: Unsigned integer. Its width is 32 bits. Primitive values copy implicitly. Numeric conversions use as or try_from; checked operations reject invalid integer arithmetic.
methods: Fallible numeric conversion; succeeds only when the input value is exactly representable. Conversion failures use the compiler-generated IntegerConversionError.

items.name: u64
items.description: Unsigned integer. Its width is 64 bits. Primitive values copy implicitly. Numeric conversions use as or try_from; checked operations reject invalid integer arithmetic.
methods: Fallible numeric conversion; succeeds only when the input value is exactly representable. Conversion failures use the compiler-generated IntegerConversionError.

items.name: f32
items.description: IEEE 754 single-precision floating point. Its width is 32 bits. Primitive values copy implicitly. Numeric conversions use as or try_from; checked operations reject invalid integer arithmetic.
methods: Fallible numeric conversion; succeeds only when the input value is exactly representable. Conversion failures use the compiler-generated IntegerConversionError.

items.name: f64
items.description: IEEE 754 double-precision floating point and the default float-literal type. Its width is 64 bits. Primitive values copy implicitly. Numeric conversions use as or try_from; checked operations reject invalid integer arithmetic.
methods: Fallible numeric conversion; succeeds only when the input value is exactly representable. Conversion failures use the compiler-generated IntegerConversionError.

items.name: bool
items.description: Boolean value; conditions require bool. Primitive values copy implicitly. Numeric conversions use as or try_from; checked operations reject invalid integer arithmetic.

items.name: usize
items.description: Unsigned pointer-width integer selected from the compilation target. Primitive values copy implicitly. Numeric conversions use as or try_from; checked operations reject invalid integer arithmetic.
methods: Fallible numeric conversion; succeeds only when the input value is exactly representable. Conversion failures use the compiler-generated IntegerConversionError.

items.name: unit
items.description: The unit result. Omitting a function return type and writing () explicitly have the same meaning.

items.name: array
items.description: Inline fixed-size storage. N is part of the type and known at compile time. Index values are checked before access; element access preserves the ordinary move/borrow rules.

items.name: slice
items.description: A borrowed contiguous view carrying a data address and element count. It retains its target lifetime. Slicing checks both bounds; mutable views require mutation permission.
methods: Returns the number of visible elements.

items.name: str
items.description: A borrowed UTF-8 byte sequence. Literals have static storage. Slice boundaries must be UTF-8 boundaries. It does not own or free the referenced text.
methods: Returns the source-defined borrowed splitting iterator.
Validates UTF-8 without copying; the returned text view retains the input byte storage lifetime.

items.name: fn
items.signature: fn(P1, P2) R / &fn(P1, P2) R / &mut fn(P1, P2) R
items.description: An owned callable or an explicit shared/mutable callable borrow. Closure parameters are explicitly typed; result types may be inferred. Captures take effect at construction. Copy captures copy automatically; non-Copy captures require move. Borrowed captures must not outlive their targets.

items.name: A
items.description: An owned allocation descriptor retaining its source pool and a stable payload address. Moving the descriptor transfers cleanup responsibility. Dropping it cleans the payload and releases its slot.
methods: Borrows the payload, unlike &allocation which borrows the descriptor.

items.name: Option
items.description: Some(T) or None. Match and if let inspect its variant. ? propagates None; postfix ! extracts Some or terminates on None. Empty/primitive-payload enums follow the implicit-copy rule.

items.name: Result
items.description: Ok(T) or Err(E). ? returns the error from the enclosing function, resolving Outer::from(Inner) when error types differ. Postfix ! extracts Ok or terminates on Err.

items.name: Pool
items.description: Fixed-capacity typed storage on the datastack. The pool must outlive its allocations. Enum pools maintain dedicated storage per variant. Neither slot allocation nor exhaustion implies an unbounded heap fallback.
methods: fn new(&mut self, value: T) A<T>
Evaluates and moves a value into a slot; terminates on exhaustion. new({...}) uses contextual initialization; new() requires valid defaults.
fn try(&mut self, value: T) Result<A<T>, PoolError>
Fallible slot allocation; Full reports exhaustion. The supplied value is consumed on both paths.

items.name: Vector
items.description: An owned descriptor for a contiguous sequence whose payload grows inside a bounded region. Construct through a Pool<Vector<T>>. Structural mutation retains all element ownership and reference dependencies.
methods: Appends by value, moving non-Copy values.
fn remove(&mut self, index: usize) T
Checks the index, extracts an element and shifts the tail.
Extracts the final element, or returns None.

items.name: HashMap
items.description: A region-backed map with integer/bool keys. Payload entries remain in place while the lookup index is reorganized. Extracted values retain their dependencies.
methods: fn insert(&mut self, key: K, value: V) Option<V>
Moves key/value into the map and returns the previous value on replacement. Primitives copy implicitly.
Borrows an existing value without consuming the key.
fn get_mut(&mut self, key: &K) Option<&mut V>

items.name: String
items.description: String owns region-backed UTF-8 bytes and is constructed through a String pool. String<N> instead has a compile-time maximum byte size and inline storage; its source-defined implementation is BoundedString<N>. Neither permits invalid UTF-8. Allocation and borrowing obligations remain visible.
methods: Appends encoded text within the applicable region budget.
Returns borrowed text pieces; the source must remain alive.

items.name: Future
items.description: Each async definition has its own compiler-generated state type, addressed by that definition’s qualified name. Construction captures immediately; .await drives it to completion and yields R. Suspension state retains live values, ownership and dependencies. The compiler/runtime polling contract uses id() and poll(ctx); this does not introduce an arbitrary dynamic trait object.

items.name: Handle
items.description: A launched execution handle. join() blocks in a synchronous context and yields Result<T, runtime::Error>. Branch contracts and captured dependencies determine required lifetime bounds; the handle name alone is not a synchronization marker.
methods: Waits for completion and transfers the result. A synchronous join is refused in async code.

items.name: AsyncHandle
items.description: The asynchronous waiting handle produced by spawn_blocking. Awaiting it yields Result<T, runtime::Error> without blocking the async poller. Captured dependencies stay reserved until the wait finishes.
methods: Waits asynchronously and transfers the completed result.

items.name: Error
items.description: Execution failures are distinct from the task’s business result. LaunchFailed is reported by waiting on the handle; failure paths still perform the required cleanup.

items.name: Context
items.description: Polling context provided by the runtime. It carries the wake registration used when returning Pending. This page describes a compiler/runtime contract, not a user-defined replacement-runtime interface.

items.name: Poll
items.description: Pending or Ready(T) in the compiler/runtime polling contract. Pending must be paired with wake registration so a notification cannot be lost.

items.name: spawn
items.description: Moves an async task into runtime scheduling and returns immediately. The task satisfies the statically resolved polling contract.

items.name: spawn_blocking
items.description: Launches blocking work from async code and returns an asynchronous waiting handle.

items.name: thread
items.description: Creates a native thread for the directly supplied synchronous block. Captures obey the ordinary ownership, lifetime and transfer contracts.

items.name: process_args
items.description: Compiler hook backing std::env::args; use the STD API in application code.

items.name: wait_socket
items.description: Restricted STD readiness hook. It is not an unrestricted application API.

items.name: copy
items.description: Explicit primitive copy. Primitive assignment, argument passing and eligible enum values also copy implicitly under the current rules.

items.name: drop
items.description: Consumes an owned value, invokes its destructor once, then cleans owned fields/elements from leaves to root. Scope exit uses the same cleanup path.

items.name: print
items.description: Compiler-provided output used by examples. It does not implicitly turn an owned value into a borrow.

items.name: addr
items.description: Raw address extraction is restricted to @unchecked. Address provenance cannot escape that block, including through usize.

items.name: references
items.description: Universal explicit borrow helpers. A<T> and types declaring these methods can expose their payload through them. * resolves declared ref()/mut_ref() according to read/write context; no permission is fabricated.

items.name: conversions
items.description: Numeric conversions are checked against the destination. try_from reports failure; as terminates when the value is not exactly representable.

items.name: tuple
items.description: A fixed-layout product. Types are inferred by position. Numeric fields (.0, .1, ...) and destructuring use the same move and borrow rules as other aggregates.

items.name: type
items.signature: #(type: T) / #(type: S<V> with { fn next(&mut self) Option<V>; })
items.description: Introduces static type parameters and method-shape requirements. with permits additional methods; without with the declared method shape is exact. No dynamic trait object is introduced.

items.name: branch
items.description: Marks a separately progressing branch. The declared join point lets analysis establish when captured references stop being used. Without join, termination may remain unbounded.

items.name: lock
items.description: A trusted synchronization contract. Object-level lock applies to public instance methods; same-object re-entry is rejected. through_result extends the protected interval through the returned object. The annotation generates no actual lock implementation.

items.name: thread
items.description: Prevents transfer to another thread. The restriction propagates through owned fields, captures and async state. Other types are transferable by default, subject to their dependencies.

items.name: configurable
items.description: Marks a package or associated constant as configurable through a lexical override. Associated constants use their qualified Type::NAME identity.

items.name: override
items.description: Specializes configurable constants in the annotated scope without a dynamic settings object.

items.name: if
items.description: Selects source before import resolution. target.os, target.family, target.arch, target.pointer_width and target.endian describe the compilation target. Excluded imports create no collisions.

items.name: datastack
items.description: Optional program memory budgets. Properties are optional. Sizes use positive decimal K/M/G units (powers of 1024). Known maximums may be inferred; unknown bounds use the documented defaults.

items.name: stack_region
items.description: A local growing-region budget; count is optional. Moves preserve the applicable capacity/lifetime constraints.

items.name: free_pages
items.description: Requests page restitution at the annotated scope’s cleanup boundary. Cleanup and cursor recovery precede OS page release.

items.name: unchecked
items.description: An explicitly unchecked boundary. Native C/assembly and raw addresses require developer-owned correctness; checked reference/ownership guarantees are not inferred for arbitrary native effects.

items.name: asm
items.description: Inline assembly with explicit instructions and bound Corbo operands. The assembly implementation owns its register preservation and raw memory effects within @unchecked.

items.name: c
items.description: Inline C with header paths and scalar/aggregate operands. corbo_runtime.h exposes runtime operations and generated C representations. Used inside @unchecked.

items.name: operators
items.description: Checked integer operations, same-type arithmetic and value-checked indices. && and || short-circuit. Signed right shifts preserve sign. Shift counts are checked. Assignment variants evaluate their destination once.

items.name: propagation
items.description: Postfix ? propagates Result/Option failure; postfix ! unwraps or terminates. Prefix ! remains boolean negation.

items.name: reference
items.description: A non-owning reference with read or mutation permission. The target and allocation source must remain valid through every use. Access compatibility, shared-lock contracts and branch join lifetimes are checked separately from the permission itself.

items.name: assignment
items.description: Assignment copies primitive and eligible enum values, otherwise transfers ownership. Compound assignments evaluate the destination once and retain the arithmetic, conversion and shift checks.

items.name: IntegerConversionError
items.description: Compiler-generated failure type for primitive try_from conversions. A failed exact numeric conversion produces this error.
